connectionGuide.purpose: One end of the 220Ω current-limiting resistor. Resistors are not polarized, so either pin can connect to either side of the circuit.
warnings: This 220Ω resistor is typically used with LEDs to limit current
For a 3.3V Pico with a red LED (~1.8V), this gives about 7mA - safe and bright
troubleshooting: Resistors have no polarity - you can connect either end to the signal
If LED is too dim, try a lower value resistor (but not below 100Ω)
If LED burns out, try a higher value resistor

connectionGuide.purpose: Other end of the 220Ω current-limiting resistor. Connect this to the LED's anode or the GPIO pin - either direction works.
warnings: This 220Ω resistor is typically used with LEDs to limit current
Without this resistor, the LED will draw too much current and may burn out
troubleshooting: Resistors have no polarity - you can connect either end to the signal
Common circuit: GPIO → Resistor → LED Anode → LED Cathode → GND
Alternative: GPIO → LED Anode → LED Cathode → Resistor → GND (also works)

warnings: Ensure power dissipation does not exceed 0.25W
At high temperatures, derate power rating
